newsitem.title: USA: Mead Q3 reflects prices, sees mixed recovery.
newsitem.headline: Mead Q3 reflects prices, sees mixed recovery.

text.p: Mead Corp said Wednesday that earnings for the third quarter 1996 reflected weaker market prices for pulp, paper and corrugating medium, and added that it sees "a mixed recovery" from its current depressed markets.
In a release Wednesday Mead said that it expects strengthening in some areas and continued instability in others as it continues to focus on controllables and value-added products.
The company said that although sales and earnings were below last year's third quarter, demand for many of Mead's products continued to strengthen.
It added that despite continued weak markets, the company's shipments of coated paper "reached record levels" and that its mills and facilities "operated very well" during the quarter.
Mead reported a net income of $62.7 million, or $1.18 per share, for the third quarter 1996, compared to net income $104.5 million, or $1.91 per share, for the third quarter last year.
Sales for the quarter were $1.23 billion, down from last year's $1.35 billion.
